o1.biggest_strength: It finds the real leak, gives one clear plan, shows the revenue and downgrade risk, and tests Team cannibalization before a full launch.
o1.biggest_mistake: It underplays the broader yearly-billing opportunity; the yearly push is only attached to the new plan rather than being a larger near-term retention lever.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add a simple honest yearly-billing follow-up for existing monthly customers, tighten the churn measurement window, and make the Agency guardrails even clearer so Team is protected.

o2.biggest_strength: The per-1,000-customer revenue math is very clear and useful, and the customer messaging sounds transparent and Buffer-like.
o2.biggest_mistake: It does not test Team downgrades before launch, even though cannibalizing Team is the main financial risk; it also dismisses yearly billing too quickly.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Include Team 8+ customers in the test before public launch, add a clear yearly-billing nudge, and clean up the month-6 math labels so every number is unambiguous.

reason: I would rather use Output 1 because it catches the biggest risk before launch and gives me a fuller company-level case. Output 2 has excellent math, but I would not launch without testing Team cannibalization first.
